claim: A financial institution assumes an affirmative duty of care when its employees undertake specific oral assurances regarding the security of a depositor's funds, and failure to honor those assurances may constitute actionable negligence independent of any contractual claim. The Third Circuit held that Harborview's repeated representations to Zembicki created a special relationship sufficient to sustain a negligence duty-of-care theory at the pleading stage.
citation: Zembicki v. Harborview Bank & Trust, 883 F.3d 541 (3d Cir. 2018)
initial_reasoning: In Zembicki v. Harborview Bank & Trust, the Third Circuit held that the bank did not owe a duty of care to the depositor at the pleading stage, rejecting the negligence claim. The court found no special relationship that created such a duty, contrary to the claim that repeated oral assurances established a negligence duty.
